content.text: This document outlines the refactoring plan for modifying the hello_world endpoint to return a random UUID and updating the search_monolith endpoint to require this UUID. Additionally, it updates the callers of the /search endpoint to use the new UUID parameter.

The current architecture includes a hello_world endpoint and a search_monolith endpoint. The user wants to introduce a UUID mechanism where the /search endpoint requires a UUID obtained from the /hello_world endpoint.

Introducing a UUID mechanism will enhance the security and traceability of requests to the /search endpoint. It ensures that each search request is uniquely identifiable, which can be useful for logging and auditing purposes.

The existing architecture includes several functions and API calls as described in the context. The hello_world endpoint returns a JSON response, and the search_monolith endpoint processes search queries.

The proposed architecture modifies the hello_world endpoint to return a UUID. The search_monolith endpoint is updated to require this UUID as a parameter. Additionally, the client code is updated to handle the new UUID mechanism.

Modify the hello_world endpoint in Repo1/app.py to return a random UUID.
Update the search_monolith endpoint in Repo1/app.py to require a UUID parameter.
Modify the call_search_api function in Repo2/client.py to first call the hello_world endpoint and then use the obtained UUID when calling the search_monolith endpoint.
Test the updated endpoints to ensure that they work correctly with the new UUID mechanism.
